model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 6 presents a comparative visualization of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across five distinct gating configurations, organized into five horizontal rows, each representing a different experimental condition. The x-axis across all subplots is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to 20, marked at intervals of 5, indicating discrete neural network layer indices. The y-axis varies by row: Rows 1–3 share a y-axis labeled “Mass,” ranging from 0 to 400, while Rows 4–5 share a y-axis labeled “Best token,” ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. In Row 1 (Baseline), a red line with circular markers shows a sharp increase in “Mass” after Layer 6, peaking near Layer 10 and again near Layer 20, with a visible dip around Layer 15. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) displays a green line with triangular markers that remains near zero across all layers, indicating minimal activation. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) shows a blue line with square markers that mirrors Row 2’s low activation but exhibits small upward spikes near Layers 10 and 20. Rows 4 and 5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) each display a single blue line without markers: Row 4 shows a steep rise in “Best token” from near 0.0 to 1.0 by Layer 5, then remains flat; Row 5 shows a similar rise but with a slight decline after Layer 15. All lines are solid, and no gridlines or error bars are visible. The figure’s caption explicitly links visual patterns to textual interpretations, such as “significant massive activations” or “no attention sinks,” but the visual data itself only depicts numerical trends across layers without labeling attention sink events directly on the plots.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations, with each row representing a distinct configuration and its corresponding activation behavior plotted against layer index. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 25, marked at intervals of 5, and uses a linear scale to indicate the depth of the model’s layers. The y-axis, labeled “Max,” ranges from 0 to 400, also on a linear scale, and quantifies the maximum activation magnitude observed at each layer. In Row 1 (Baseline), a red line with triangular markers and a solid style rises sharply after Layer 6, reaching a peak near 400 around Layer 10, then drops and rises again near Layer 20, exhibiting the “attention sink” behavior described in the caption. Row 2 (SDPA Gating) displays a green line with circular markers and a solid style that remains near zero across all layers, indicating suppressed activations and absence of attention sinks. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) shows a blue line with square markers and a solid style that mirrors the green line’s low activation profile but exhibits small, residual peaks near Layers 10 and 20, consistent with “residual attention sinks.” Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) depict a black line with diamond markers and a solid style that closely follows the red line’s trajectory, rising sharply after Layer 6, peaking near 400, and showing similar oscillatory behavior, indicating a return to baseline-level massive activations and attention sinks.
model_annotations.English: Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations, illustrated through two line plots arranged horizontally at the bottom of the figure. The left plot, labeled “Mass,” has an x-axis labeled “Layer” ranging from 0 to approximately 25 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and a y-axis labeled “Mass” ranging from 0 to 400 with tick marks at intervals of 100. This plot contains three lines: a red line with circular markers that starts near 0, sharply rises to approximately 400 at layer 6, remains high until layer 20, then drops; a green line with triangular markers that remains near 0 until layer 10, then rises to approximately 300 at layer 20, and drops slightly afterward; and a blue line with square markers that stays near 0 across all layers. The right plot, labeled “Best token,” has an x-axis also labeled “Layer” ranging from 0 to approximately 25 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and a y-axis labeled “Best token” ranging from 0.0 to 0.2 with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. This plot contains a single blue line with square markers that remains near 0.0 until layer 5, then rises sharply to approximately 0.2 at layer 10, and remains flat until layer 20, after which it drops slightly. The caption below the plots explains that Row 1 (Baseline) shows significant massive activations and attention sinks after the 6th layer; Row 2 (SDPA Gating) shows reduced activations and no attention sinks; Row 3 (Value Layer Gating) shows similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks; and Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) show massive activations and attention sinks resembling the baseline.
model_annotations.German: Figure 6 presents a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations, with two subplots arranged horizontally. The left subplot displays “Mass” on the y-axis, ranging from 0 to 400 in linear increments of 100, and “Layer” on the x-axis, ranging from 0 to 20 in linear increments of 5. A red line with triangular markers rises sharply to approximately 400 at layer 6, remains near that level until layer 18, then drops to 0 at layer 20. A green line with circular markers remains near 0 until layer 18, then rises to approximately 300 at layer 20. A blue line with square markers remains near 0 across all layers. The right subplot displays “Residual attention sink” on the y-axis, ranging from 0.0 to 0.2 in linear increments of 0.05, and “Layer” on the x-axis, ranging from 0 to 20 in linear increments of 5. A single blue line with square markers remains near 0 until layer 6, then rises to approximately 0.15 at layer 8, remains stable until layer 18, then drops back to 0 at layer 20.
